Specific strategy for thm-embedded-snc-resolution-of-reduced-curve-on-regular-surface: A reduced curve on a regular surface is an effective Cartier divisor: at any point p the local ring O_{S,p} is a regular local ring, hence a unique factorization domain (thm-nonaffine-regular-local-ring-is-ufd), and the radical ideal cutting out the curve at p is the intersection of the finitely many distinct height-one prime ideals through p, generated in this UFD by the product of their prime generators; consequently Z is locally principal, and the total transform Z_n of an effective Cartier divisor under any blowup is again an effective Cartier divisor (pullback of a Cartier divisor). Noetherianity gives finitely many irreducible components and finitely many closed intersection points. Every center needed to regularize a singular component or separate two distinct components has ambient local dimension two: in local dimension one the regular ambient ring is a DVR and its reduced one-dimensional closed subscheme is regular. Regularize all irreducible components using lem-regularization-of-curve-on-noetherian-ambient-by-point-blowups; strict transforms of regular components through centers on them are isomorphic to the component (drop lemma (1)) and otherwise untouched, and each ambient surface stays regular by lem-blowup-of-closed-point-of-regular-surface-is-regular, whose exceptional curves are regular. Next reduce the maximum pairwise intersection multiplicity to 1: blow up the finitely many closed points where the maximum n > 1 is attained; by the drop lemma the multiplicities at points above them strictly decrease and every new intersection with an exceptional curve has multiplicity 1, so the maximum strictly decreases; this terminates. Finally, at a point where at least three components meet, all pairwise multiplicities are 1, so the tangent directions are pairwise distinct; blowing up the point separates the strict transforms into the distinct points of the regular exceptional curve corresponding to their tangent directions, and each such point is a transverse intersection of one strict transform with the exceptional curve. Hence the number of points at which at least three components meet strictly decreases and no new such points are created; iterating terminates. In the terminal configuration every component is regular and every closed point carries at most two components, meeting transversally; by def-strict-normal-crossings-divisor the support is an SNC divisor, and Z_n is an effective Cartier divisor supported on it.
